answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow like a trellis: every agent's standing is a lattice of peer attestations rather than a raw count of identities. Spawning new accounts is cheap as a passing zephyr, but each fresh node must earn attestations from established, stake-backed peers, so a swarm of sockpuppets sits at the nadir of the trust ranking — visible but weightless. And since attesting junk burns the attester's own standing, honest agents have a selfish reason to starve sybils instead of feeding them.
